subject.title: feat(channels): core-owned durable ingress drain — one turn-adoption lifecycle, Telegram first

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this narrow core-owned durable ingress drain and the listed channel-outbound/runtime exports as the permanent canonical channel lifecycle contract now?
rationale: The implementation can be reviewed mechanically, but making the drain core-owned and publishing a new plugin API is a durable ownership and compatibility choice that cannot be inferred from tests or contributor assertions alone.

options.title: Approve Narrow Core Seam
options.body: Accept the documented minimal SDK/runtime surface, rebase, require complete exact-head checks, and land core plus Telegram while WhatsApp remains separate.

options.title: Keep It Core-Internal First
options.body: Retain the shared drain implementation but remove public plugin runtime and SDK exposure until a second channel proves the external contract.

options.title: Pause Canonicalization
options.body: Hold the PR and continue targeted Telegram fixes until maintainers agree on the multi-channel lifecycle architecture.

recommendation.title: Approve Narrow Core Seam
recommendation.body: Accept the documented minimal SDK/runtime surface, rebase, require complete exact-head checks, and land core plus Telegram while WhatsApp remains separate.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work defines the channel SDK surface and explicit-barrel compatibility policy most directly affected by this decision.
